meta.guide_tau: Level caption:  energy (NIST, or a measurement of the last 20 years where one exists) and measured lifetime (where one exists).
meta.notes: Nd I lifetimes (second pass): 15 levels measured by Biemont et al. 2004 (opened, Lund University repository) and 84 lifetimes of Den Hartog, Fittante, Lawler 2011 read second-hand in two open theses (Ryder 2011 Table 5.2; Putnam 2014 Table 6.1) (method "compilation", no uncertainty printed; the original abstract quotes +/-5%). Where both exist the directly opened Biemont value is the entry and the Den Hartog value sits under the level key "alternatives" (each alternative names its quantity), except for 20300.875 cm^-1 where the Biemont value fails the tau x sum(A) check (see conflicts). Lifetimes were checked against the NIST A values: tau x sum(A) <= 0.96 for all drawn levels except those listed under conflicts. The branching-fraction paper (Stockett 2011) and the ground-term hyperfine paper (Childs & Goodman 1972) remain closed. Hyperfine A constants are for the even-parity metastable levels 7L5, 7L11, 7K4 (second-hand) and the ground level 5I4 of 143Nd (abstract of the original paper). Nuclear spins 7/2 for 143Nd and 145Nd from the IAEA/ENSDF ground-state table (https://nds.iaea.org/relnsd/v1/data?fields=ground_states&nuclides=143nd). Third pass (2026-10-02): added (a) 38 Nd I lifetimes read directly in Gorshkov et al., Astrophysics 17, 437 (1982), Table 1 (Springer free preview): 3 levels that had no lifetime get it as the entry (19590.241, 22229.000, 23562.766), 2 second-hand quotes of the same numbers are replaced by the direct reading with uncertainty (19700.856, 25478.135), the rest sit under "alternatives" beside the laser-based values; (b) isotope shifts of 8 Nd I lines (567.6-630.2 nm) from van Leeuwen et al., Z. Phys. A 301, 95 (1981), Table 1, stored with keys written heavier-lighter (e.g. "144-142" = nu(144) - nu(142)) so that the printed sign is kept; the printed errors are three times the statistical error; (c) isotope shifts of the 562.2 nm line relative to 150Nd, second-hand (Suryanarayana 2022 quoting D'yachkov 2018), the odd-isotope values being calculated, not measured. The NIST lines file carries A values for only 9 Nd I lines, so the tau x sum(A) check could be applied only to the upper levels of those lines.
